title: Jensen Huang Is Back at Nvidia After 11 Days. OpenAI and Disney Have Seen Sudden Returns Before.
excerpt: Sudden returns of a former chief executive have happened before at large technology and media companies: OpenAI agreed to bring back Sam Altman four days after removing him in November 2023, and Disney's shares rose as much as 10% when it re-appointed Bob Iger in November 2022. Nvidia reinstated its co-founder Jensen Huang on 23 November 2026, eleven days after he resigned, and its shares rose more than 31% that day; these cases show how such comebacks have unfolded, not how this one will.

title: Ether Is Two-Thirds Below Its Record. It Has Fallen Further Twice Before.
excerpt: Ether traded at about $1,680 on 21 November, roughly two-thirds below its August 2025 record of about $4,947. It has fallen further twice before, by 94% in 2018 and 81% in 2022, and each time it took roughly three to four years to regain its previous peak.

title: 1st Edition Charizard Has Reportedly Passed $1 Million. Its Last Record Stood for Almost Four Years.
excerpt: A PSA 10 1st Edition Base Set Charizard was reported in October 2026 to have sold for $1,385,274, two and a half times the $550,000 record set only ten months earlier. The card has been through a run like this once before: it climbed from under $20,000 in 2017 to $420,000 in March 2022, and that record then stood for almost four years.

title: Silver Is More Than 60% Below Its January Record. Here Is What Followed the 1980 and 2011 Peaks.
excerpt: Silver has fallen this far from a record twice before: after it peaked near $50 in January 1980 and in April 2011, it fell to $10.80 within ten weeks in 1980 and to $13.695 by December 2015, and neither peak was surpassed until October 2025. Silver was trading near $41.86 on 20 November, more than 60% below its late-January record, and this time the stated driver is expected US rate rises rather than an exchange crackdown, so the precedents describe past paths rather than a forecast.

title: Nvidia Has Lost Its Founder as CEO. Here Is What Followed Earlier Tech Leadership Changes.
excerpt: Sudden changes at the top of large technology companies have been followed by very different paths: Apple's shares fell about 5% after hours when Steve Jobs resigned as chief executive in 2011, and the company later became the first listed company worth $1 trillion, while Intel's shares jumped 15% when it named a permanent chief executive a little over three months after Pat Gelsinger's exit. Nvidia, whose co-founder Jensen Huang resigned on 12 November 2026 after 33 years, is at the start of that process, with an interim chief executive and a search under way, so these cases show a range of outcomes rather than a forecast.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Have Lost $2.35bn in November. Here Is What Followed Earlier Outflow Waves.
excerpt: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $2.35 billion in the first nine trading days of November, leaving them about $1.98 billion in net outflows for 2026. Earlier waves ended differently: bitcoin set new records within months of the January 2024 and early 2025 outflows, but was still lower a year after the record withdrawals of late 2025.

snapItems.label: November outflows after nine trading days (The Block)

title: Art Academy Promo Cards Now Sell for Millions. Has a Contest Prize Card Done This Before?
excerpt: Yes, once: the Pikachu Illustrator, a prize card from a 1998 illustration contest, went from $195,000 in 2019 to $16.49 million at auction in February 2026. The 2015 Art Academy contest promos have made a comparable jump in months rather than years, but each design was printed in a run of 100 copies and their sales record at these prices is only a few months old.

title: New York Art Auctions Are Aiming for $2bn Again. Here Is How the Last Two Slumps Ended.
excerpt: The art market has recovered from two deep slumps in living memory: after 1990 sales stayed far below their peak for years, while after the 2008 crisis a new auction record for a painting came in May 2010. New York's November sales are now forecast at $2.04bn or more after auction sales fell 25% in 2024, and the speed of this year's rebound is what sets it apart.

title: Anthropic's IPO Could Be the Biggest Ever. Here Is What Followed Earlier Record Listings.
excerpt: Record listings have started strongly before and then struggled: Alibaba in 2014 and Saudi Aramco in 2019 both rose sharply on debut, then fell below their offer prices within a year, while SpaceX, the record holder since June 2026, ended its first week 37% above its IPO price. Anthropic’s offering, which with $26 billion of share commitments would come to about $90 billion, has not yet priced, so these precedents show a range of outcomes rather than a forecast.

title: Bitcoin Has Slipped Below Its 200-Week Average. Here Is What Followed Earlier Breaks.
excerpt: Bitcoin fell below its 200-week moving average, around $68,000, on 13 November and kept falling, to about $63,500 late on 14 November. The line has been tested before: it held on a weekly-close basis in December 2018, was broken only briefly in March 2020, and in 2022 bitcoin stayed below it until October 2023, after a further fall to $15,480.

title: PSA Has Reopened Its Value Grading Tier. In 2021, It Took 14 Months to Return.
excerpt: PSA reopened its Value grading tier on 29 October 2026 at $39.99 per card, just under five months after pausing it with about 10 million cards in its backlog. It has done this once before: in 2021 PSA suspended its cheaper services for the same reason, and Value only returned in June 2022, about 14 months later, after Express had come back $50 dearer.

title: Pre-Owned Watch Prices Are Rising Again. Here Is How the Last Two Watch Slumps Ended.
excerpt: The watch industry has climbed out of two slumps since 2008: Swiss watch exports rebounded 22.1% in 2010 after falling 22.3% in 2009, but rose only 2.7% in 2017 after two years of decline. Pre-owned prices have now risen for five straight quarters yet remain about 29% below their 2022 peak, and record inventory is what sets this recovery apart.

title: AI Stocks Just Had Their Worst Day Since 2025. Two Earlier Tech Scares Ended Very Differently.
excerpt: Yes, tech has been through scares like this before: Nvidia's record one-day loss in the DeepSeek sell-off of January 2025 was regained within five months, while the telecom build-out bust of 2000 to 2002 took the Nasdaq down 78.4% and fifteen years to recover. The sell-off of 5 November 2026, driven by worries that AI data-centre construction may slow, has so far looked more like a sharp scare than either of those, but the precedents show both endings are possible.

title: Airdrop Farming Is Back in Fashion. What Happened to the Big Airdrops Before?
excerpt: Past airdrops have more often been followed by falling prices than rising ones: Uniswap's token rose in its first week in 2020, but Arbitrum and Wormhole traded well below their early highs within days, and a Keyrock study found 88% of tokens launched alongside airdrops in 2024 declined. Vendor research on this year's airdrops points the same way, with 35 of 46 tokens studied trading below their first-week median price.

title: Delta Reign Puts Mega Rayquaza Back at the Centre. Rayquaza Has Been Here Twice Before.
excerpt: Yes: Delta Reign, released on 6 November 2026, is not the first English Pokémon set to put Rayquaza up front, after Roaring Skies featured Mega Rayquaza in 2015 and a Rayquaza VMAX became one of the most valuable cards in Evolving Skies in 2021. The earlier sets show that a Rayquaza headline is no guarantee the set's top card will be a Rayquaza, and they arrived in very different markets.

title: Gold Has Fallen Far From Its January Record. Here Is What Followed Its Last Two Peaks.
excerpt: Gold has been here before: after its peaks in January 1980 and September 2011, it did not set a new record until January 2008 and July 2020. Spot gold is now near $4,070, well below January's record of about $5,595, and the speed and causes of this year's swing differ from both precedents in ways worth understanding.

title: OpenAI's New Round Came In Below Its First Target. Tech Has Been Here Before.
excerpt: Yes: Facebook in 2012, Uber in 2019 and WeWork in 2019 all priced below what had been expected, and what followed ranged from a slow recovery to bankruptcy. OpenAI's reported $11 billion raise at a $1.25 trillion valuation, below the $1.4 trillion target reported in September, is a private round rather than a listing, which changes how far those precedents carry.

title: Democrats Won the Midterms. What Have US Elections Meant for Crypto Before?
excerpt: US elections have mattered to crypto mainly through what Congress and regulators do next, and the last two showed how differently that can play out: a policy-driven rally after 2024, and an industry collapse unrelated to the vote in the same week as the 2022 midterms. The 2026 result, with Democrats taking both the House and the Senate, puts the stalled CLARITY Act at the centre of that question.

title: 30th Celebration Brings Back Base Set Charizard. Pokémon Has Done This Twice Before.
excerpt: Yes: the 30th Celebration set is the third time in a decade that Pokémon has marked an anniversary by bringing back its most famous early designs, after Evolutions in 2016 and Celebrations in 2021. The precedents show how differently each set was built and sold, and the 2021 one arrived in a year so heated that a major US retailer temporarily stopped selling trading cards in its stores.

title: Why Recency Carries as Much Weight as Frequency in CIA Scoring
